subject: Recap & next steps: pilot economics / ops alignment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novusai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: inference economics & pilot success criteria (today's call)

Oliver — thanks for the time earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. High level takeaways below: 

Pain points we heard
- Unit economics are the top constraint: model compute is ~62% of your LLM spend and is driving runway concerns.
- Latency spikes (P95 ~150–200ms) on production traffic are causing UX regressions for search and chat.
- No shared KV/prefix cache today; app-level batching is custom and brittle.

Current stack (from your description)
- HF Transformers on k8s over GPU VMs (mixed T4 / A10-like pools)
- App-side semaphore-based batching (peak batch sizes 1–4)
- No persistent KV cache; short-lived in-process caches per pod

Success criteria for a Redwood pilot (you suggested)
- Achieve >=40% reduction in $/inference (unit cost) for the tested workload OR reduce monthly spend by 30% while matching quality.
- Stabilize P95 latency to <=120ms for the primary chat endpoint.
- Demonstrate safe quantization path with <1% downstream metric delta on your reranking eval set.

Technical openness you flagged
- Comfortable evaluating int8 quantization; 4-bit (Q4) is interesting but requires evaluation against your rerank/LLM-quality set.
- Willing to test prefix/KV caching and Redwood's automatic batching (we suggested batched sizes up to 32 tokens for generator requests).

Immediate next steps
1) You share a 48–72h sample of production traces (we requested token-level counts + request/response latencies) — I attached a CSV with the minimal fields we need.
2) Redwood team (Marissa + Aditya) will draft a 6-week pilot SOW and measurable KPIs (cost delta, P95 latency, quality guardrails).
3) We set a follow-up to lock scope and data transfers (target next week).

Attachments: pilot-info-request.csv (small CSV with fields to populate)

If I missed anything important from your side, flag it and we’ll adjust. Otherwise we’ll follow up with the SOW and a short ops checklist for the trace export.

— Marcus Lin
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference


On Fri, Dec 5, 2026 at 14:05 Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novusai.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marcus — good call. A couple clarifications embedded below.
>
>

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novusai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: inference economics & pilot success criteria (today's call)

Marcus — appreciate the recap. A few numbered clarifications so we are precise: 

1) Numbers: Our infra line for model-serving is $0.85/token-equivalent on average (includes instance amortization + model runtime). The business asks for a 30–40% improvement over the next 3 months to keep the project funded.
2) Throughput & traffic shape: Baseline traffic is ~120 rps across two endpoints; median prompt length ~45 tokens; 95th percentile prompt length ~420 tokens (long-tailed).
3) Latency: P95 target of <=120ms is correct for the chat endpoint. We will accept slightly higher tail for rerank (~200–250ms) if unit costs drop materially.
4) Quantization: Open to int8 immediately. 4-bit is allowed for an experimental arm if Redwood provides clear rollback criteria and quality checks.
5) Security/compliance: We will need a SOC2 questionnaire answered and an IP/data handling clause in the SOW. Procurement timeline: we hope to be contracted by mid-Jan if pilot outcomes look promising.

I uploaded a small trace sample to the folder linked below and attached a 5k-sample tar for the pilot team.

Oliver Grant
Head of ML Infrastructure, NovusAI
oliver.grant@novusai.com | +1 (617) 555-4472

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Recap: inference economics & pilot success criteria (internal)

Internal — forwarding Oliver's reply. Key asks we need to cover in the SOW:
- Pilot KPI: 30–40% unit-cost reduction target (they framed runway in both % and absolute $).
- Workload: median/95th token lengths + 120 rps baseline. Long-tail prompts (up to ~420 tokens).
- Two arms recommended: (A) quantized int8 baseline; (B) experimental Q4 with rollback gating.
- Ops: KV/prefix caching + Redwood continuous batching. Need to note TTL expectations (they are not using cache today).
- Compliance: SOC2 questionnaire + IP/data clause.

Marissa — can you draft a 6-week pilot SOW with: measurable KPIs, pilot start options (Jan 10–20), minimal data share checklist, and a single-sheet billing metric proposal (committed tokens vs per-inference vs blended)? Aditya — please prep a short runbook for the pilot that outlines batching config, cache TTLs, and quantization test harness.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the follow-up with Oliver after you both sign off on the draft.

— Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novusai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: NovusAI pilot SOW draft + ops questions

Hi Oliver — attached is a first-pass SOW draft and a short billing decision matrix. Summary of what we propose based on the call: 

Proposal highlights
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week onboarding + 3-week experiments + 1-week wrap + readout)
- Pilot arms: 
  * Arm A: int8 quantized model + Redwood batching + KV cache enabled (TTL = 1h)
  * Arm B: 4-bit experimental model (Q4) behind quality rollback with A/B canary at 5% traffic
- Batching suggestion: adaptive batching up to 32 tokens / request-window; latency SLOs per endpoint (chat P95 <=120ms).
- Billing proposal: recommend a blended committed token discount for pilot (committed token bucket for 6 weeks) — see attached decision matrix.

Open questions we need from you to finalize SOW
1) Confirm whether committed billing should be on token-equivalent or per-inference (Novus prefers token-equivalent historically).
2) Confirm the TTL expectation for KV cache (we suggested 1h but can change).
3) SOC2/questionnaire contact — send the contact for your security reviewer and any specific controls you need verified.
4) Pilot start window: you mentioned mid-Jan; what is your preferred kick date?

Attachments: novus-pilot-sow-draft.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-novus-pilot (pilot assets + trace upload)

If everything looks good we can route the SOW to procurement and DocuSign; we will include the IP/data handling clause per your request.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Principal Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0261

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@novusai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 10:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NovusAI pilot SOW draft + ops questions

Marissa / Marcus — thanks, this looks good and aligned. Quick confirmations: 

- Committed billing: token-equivalent makes the most sense for us. We can commit to a 6-week token bucket sized to ~10M tokens/week for the pilot.
- Cache TTL: 1h is fine to start.
- Security: I'll introduce you to our security reviewer (Sanjay Mehta) — copying his email: sanjay.mehta@novusai.com. Expect a short SOC2 questionnaire.
- Pilot start: Targeting Jan 15, 2027 start — procurement aiming to have the DocuSign returned by Jan 12.

I uploaded a 5k-sample trace bundle (novus-traces-sample.tar.gz) to the Drive folder and granted access. We are comfortable with the two-arm approach; please include the rollback gating criteria for Q4 in the SOW.

Looking forward to the pilot — Oliver

Attachments: novus-traces-sample.tar.gz
